Israel hit back at the UK for leading [a twelve-country alliance](https://www.lemonde.fr/en/international/article/2026/09/09/eleven-european-countries-and-canada-impose-sanctions-on-israel-over-products-from-settlements-in-the-west-bank_6757323_4.html) that is restricting trade with Israeli settlements in the West Bank, a grouping that showcases the growing closeness between Europe and Canada.Analysts said the measures against settlement building, illegal under international law, were more symbolic than tangible. But the curbs nevertheless marked the latest example of Western countries — notably excluding the US — [banding together](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-09-08/eu-and-canada-plan-far-reaching-alliance-to-strengthen-partnership) in sometimes informal groupings on issues ranging from support for Ukraine to trade.

That cooperation looks set to grow with Canada’s prime minister due to [address the European Parliament next week](https://www.euronews.com/my-europe/2026/08/26/mark-carney-to-address-european-parliament-as-canada-turns-to-brussels-amid-trumps-tariff-). Recent events have even pushed the “fringe” notion of Canadian membership in the EU “[into mainstream conversation](https://www.newyorker.com/news/global-notes/what-if-canada-joined-the-eu),” a New Yorker writer noted.

Singapore [increased its prime minister’s salary to $2.8 million](https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/sep/09/singapore-pm-ministers-salary-pay-rise), part of its longstanding strategy to boost talent and reduce corruption.For comparison, the UK’s premier earns $230,000 and the US president $400,000. Singapore’s first prime minister [argued in 1955](https://www.nas.gov.sg/archivesonline/data/pdfdoc/2000063010.htm) that low pay meant top candidates rarely joined politics and faced temptation when they did.

The city state has a carrot-and-stick model: Politicians’ pay is pegged to the country’s top 1,000 earners, but corruption is reliably punished. Whether the strategy reduces graft is a live debate — Singapore is [third-lowest of 182 countries](https://www.transparency.org/en/press/corruption-perceptions-index-2025-stalling-anti-corruption-progress-asia-pacific-public-anger-surges) on one index, but Hong Kong, with much lower pay, also scores well. The policy does, however, [seem to make it easier](https://www.channelnewsasia.com/singapore/minister-salary-increase-recruitment-analysts-6369851) to attract qualified candidates.

France and Canada joined the UK in announcing trade sanctions on Israel’s West Bank settlements Tuesday, as [rising settler violence](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/09/08/world/europe/uk-sanctions-israel-west-bank-settlements.html) in the occupied territory widened a geopolitical rift between Israel and its allies.

They are among 12 nations that signed a letter condemning Israel for “[undermining the possibility](https://x.com/Ed_Miliband/status/2097350193679127012/photo/1) of a two-state solution.” UK foreign secretary Ed Miliband has vowed a “comprehensive reset” of relations with Israel, drawing sharp remonstrance from the White House, which [threatened trade countermeasures](https://www.politico.eu/article/us-escalates-ahead-of-uk-trade-sanctions-on-israeli-settlements/) against the UK.

London’s newfound assertiveness reflects a “post-American turn,” former UK government adviser Ben Judah argued: In marshaling a European coalition against Israeli settlements, “the UK has found a role and an influential one, partially as a consequence of [America abandoning hers](https://x.com/b_judah/status/2097381629501059128).”

One of Beijing’s top America experts wrote that the upcoming US-China summit offers a “rare opportunity” to put a floor under the countries’ relations, potentially signaling Beijing’s mindset ahead of the Washington meeting.

Whereas Beijing once rejected Washington’s framing of “strategic competition” with China, it is [now more confident](https://www.foreignaffairs.com/united-states/emerging-us-china-detente) about managing that competition, Da Wei argued in a Foreign Affairs essay that was [likely approved by Beijing](https://x.com/dennisw5/status/2096969614106267971?s=46), the CIA’s former China analysis head suggested.
